thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock-index Futures Struggle For Altitude As Midterms, Fed Policy Update Loom

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock-index Futures Struggle For Altitude As Midterms, Fed Policy Update Loom
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch
U.S. stock futures were trading virtually unchanged Monday, in a week set to be teeming with news, including an updated policy statement from the Federal Reserve and midterm elections that could alter the balance of power in Washington.
How did benchmarks fare?
Futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average were little changed at 25,244, less than 0.1% lower, while S&P 500 index futures were flat at 2,724.50 and Nasdaq-100 futures edged 0.1% higher to 6,986.
On Friday, the Dow lost 109.91 points, or 0.4%, to end at 25,270.83, the S&P 500 index fell 17.31 points, or 0.6%, to 2,723.06, and the Nasdaq Composite Index declined 77.06 points, or 1%, to 7,356.99.
For the week, both the Dow and the S&P 500 rose 2.4% and the Nasdaq advanced 2.7%, its first weekly gain since the end of September.
What drove the market?
Midterm congressional elections, which are expected to see Democrats take control of the House and Republicans maintain a grip on the Senate, take place Tuesday. On Thursday, the Fed concludes a two-day policy meeting, which isn't expected to deliver a change in rates but may offer fresh insights to investors about the pace of coming rate increases and the effects of trade clashes between the U.S. and China on the domestic economy.
On Friday, markets contended with a series of conflicting headlines on the progress of negotiations between Beijing and Washington. Stocks pared losses in late trade (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-cuts-intraday-loss-after-trump-declares-progress-on-trade-deal-with-china-directly-countering-kudlow-2018-11-02) Friday after President Donald Trump said progress was being made in talks with Chinese leadership. A few hours earlier, his top economic adviser, Larry Kudlow, said the U.S. and China were a long way from reaching a trade deal.
On Monday, China's President Xi Jinping, speaking at a trade expo in Shangha (https://www.bbc.com/news/business-46093478)i, vowed to address criticisms that its trade practices are "unfair," by reducing its tariffs and opening up its economy to more imports.
The Caixin survey of Chinese manufacturing slipped to 50.8, marking its lowest reading (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/11/05/chinas-services-sector-growth-slowest-in-13-months-caixin-survey.html) in more than a year, supporting the idea that the economy of the world's second-largest economy is slowing. A reading of at least 50 indicates improving conditions.
Read:How U.S.-China trade talks are the biggest catalyst for the stock market (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-chart-shows-why-trade-war-fears-are-the-biggest-catalyst-for-the-stock-market-2018-11-02)
Which stocks are in focus?
Shares of Apple Inc.(AAPL) shares were down 1.2% in premarket trade Monday following the iPhone maker's 6.6% stock decline on Friday, after saying it would no longer disclose (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/when-the-going-gets-tough-apple-hides-its-numbers-2018-11-01) unit sales of its products for investors, as it has for more than a decade.
What data are in focus
A reading on services from Markit for October is due at 9:45 a.m. Eastern, while a more closely nonmanufacturing report from ISM for the same month is scheduled for 10 a.m., with average estimates from economists surveyed by MarketWatch a reading of 58.6.
What are analysts saying?
"This adds weight to the argument that China's economy is cooling. Overnight, China's Xi Jinping talked about boosting global trade, and warned about the downside of protectionist policies, but the update failed to boost investor sentiment," wrote David Madden, market analyst at CMC Markets UK, in a Monday research note.
